title: Commitment framework, notice windows, and credit language for reserved throughput
creator: Anika Shah
description: Draft a single-source contract appendix and internal measurement spec that defines: (1) how reserved throughput commitments are measured, (2) error-budget computation and crediting, (3) required customer notices and remediation windows, and (4) the interaction with autoscaling/fleet controls and fallbacks. Deliverables: contractual clause text for sales + legal, implementation checklist for runtime telemetry, example customer notices, and an internal runbook for credit issuance.
acceptance_criteria: A legal-grade contract appendix (.docx text) with unambiguous definitions for 'Committed Throughput', measurement interval, and acceptable degradation thresholds
A one-page engineering measurement spec (SLO calc) that maps telemetry signals to contract metrics
Clear formulas for error-budget-to-credit conversion with examples (monthly and weekly) and a sample credit memo template
Defined notification & remediation flow: who gets notified, timing (T0,T+30m,T+4h,T+72h), and automatic vs manual escalation rules
Documentation of how autoscaling/fleet controls (burst pools, fallback models, regional failover) affect both measurement and remediation (i.e., when credits apply and when they do not)
Sign-off from Legal, Revenue Ops, and Runtime Engineering on the final language
comments: 2025-01-12 - Anika: Initial draft completed and shared with Runtime Eng. Key open questions: measurement window (5m vs 1h), whether p95 latency gating should be part of throughput SLO.

2025-01-15 - Miguel: Runtime thinks 1h rolling window smooths noisy short spikes, legal prefers 24h for contract clarity. Proposed compromise: internal telemetry computed on 5m buckets but aggregated into 24h contract windows.

2025-01-20 - Legal (review): Reworded 'degradation' to 'service degradation event' and requested explicit examples of customer actions that pause credit accrual (customer-caused traffic patterns, misconfigured ACLs, large model swaps). See legal-review link below.
2025-01-23 - Engineering PR: measurement spec and dashboards created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/928 (ops/telemetry + test vectors). Waiting on perf validation.
2025-01-28 - Revenue Ops: asked to include billing cutover language and how credits show up on invoices. Added credit memo template to artifacts.
2025-01-30 - Design: sample customer notice language added; small copy edits requested for 'SLA credit' -> 'service credit' for customer-facing docs.
2025-02-02 - Miguel: Incorporated legal edits and ops feedback; ready for exec legal sign-off. Deployment checklist for telemetry included in internal doc (Confluence).
decisions: Use 5-minute telemetry buckets for measurement granularity; contract obligations expressed as 24-hour rolling windows to avoid reacting to microbursts.

Define Committed Throughput as 'percentage of committed request-units (tokens or inference-requests depending on product SKU) successfully processed within target latency bound at or above Customer Commitment Rate' — ties throughput to latency performance.
Error budget is computed as the total minutes per month where effective throughput falls below the committed rate, converted to credit units using a deterministic formula (see examples).

Autoscaling and burst pools: if autoscaling successfully scales to meet demand but transient latency spikes occur during the scaling window (first T+2m), credits are not automatically issued; sustained failure beyond T+30m triggers credit eligibility unless the event is attributable to customer config.

Fallback to regional or lower-tier model variants is considered a remediation; if the platform enacted fallback without customer consent and throughput remained below commitment, credit applies. If customer explicitly enabled fallback via a policy, credits are reduced per the contract's 'customer-enabled mitigation' clause.
